To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed and tested a novel fluorescence-based method to detect areas of degraded collagen in tooth dentine at high resolution and that this method facilitates selection of well preserved samples for isotope analysis.

1) the autofluorescence intensity of the collagen in tooth dentine is a proxy for the state of collagen preservation, 2) the fluorescence intensity of collagen can be mapped in thin sections of human tooth dentine, 3) the state of preservation can be determined prior to sampling, and 4) the state of collagen degradation can be determined at the resolution of a single microsampling area.

the presented dual-colour fluorescence imaging approach allows detection of collagen decay in dentine at high resolution and facilitates selection of areas with well-preserved collagen ahead of sampling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for fluorescence imaging of collagen preservation in teeth.
the development of methods for the detection of collagen preservation in archaeological bone and tooth samples.
the application of new technologies in the field of paleodietary studies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the presented method allows the identification of collagen preservation prior to sampling, but that it cannot be used to identify the exact location of a sample within the dentine, which is necessary to determine the time of formation.
the fluorescence method presented here is a useful and powerful tool to detect diagenetically altered collagen at the microscopic scale, and to select well-preserved areas for microsampling.
the presented fluorescence imaging approach is an additional tool for the evaluation of the quality of the collagen preservation in the dentin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this method is an important step in the direction of improving the reliability of diachronic insights gained from isotope analysis of collagen.
the presented method is useful for screening of collagen preservation and selection of well-preserve samples prior to isotope analysis of collagen in tooth dentine.
the dual-colour autoflorescence imaging approach is a useful tool for the selection of well-perserved samples for isotope analysis.
The main takeaway from our work is that

even in dentin areas that were apparently well-preserved based on histology and SEM, collagen preservation was not optimal and that the dual-colour imaging approach can be used to select areas of optimal collagen preservation.
collagen preservation in tooth enamel is not as good as previously thought, and that diagenesis can occur at a much smaller spatial scale than previously assumed.
even areas of dentine that appear to be intact based on histological criteria may be subject to diagenetic decay and that this can be identified by fluorescence imaging.
